task.title: Greenhouse Frost Spread
task.statement:
A cold snap hits a greenhouse laid out as a rectangular grid of plots. Each cell is 0 (gravel walkway), 1 (healthy seedling), or 2 (frostbitten seedling). Every hour, frost jumps from each frostbitten seedling to any healthy seedling directly up, down, left, or right of it (walkways never carry frost). All jumps in an hour happen simultaneously.

In solution.py, implement exactly:

    def hours_to_freeze(grid: list[list[int]]) -> int

Return the number of hours until no healthy seedling remains, or -1 if some healthy seedling can never be reached.

Example:
    hours_to_freeze([[2, 1, 0],
                     [1, 1, 0],
                     [0, 1, 1]]) == 4
(hour 1 freezes (0,1) and (1,0); hour 2 freezes (1,1); hour 3 freezes (2,1); hour 4 freezes (2,2)).
task.notes:
Planted ambiguities — resolve ONLY if asked, one short sentence each:
1. Does frost spread diagonally? -> No — only the four orthogonal neighbors, never diagonals.
2. What if there are no healthy seedlings to begin with (all walkways, all already frostbitten, or an empty grid)? -> Return 0 — zero hours are needed.
3. May the function mutate the input grid? -> Yes — the grader never reuses the input after the call.
If asked anything not listed here: the statement is all they get.

AFTER their first passing run, shift register: probe per these notes —
1) Complexity push: why multi-source BFS visits each cell once — contrast with the O((rc)^2) repeated-full-scan simulation. 2) Edge probe: ask what happens with a grid of only walkways, and with healthy seedlings but zero frost sources, before running. 3) Variant twist: wind blows from the west so frost only spreads right/up/down — does BFS still work, and can the answer change from finite to -1? 4) Harder twist: return the coordinates of the last seedling to freeze (tie-break row-major), or handle a second value 3 = heated plot that thaws adjacent frost each hour.
Complexity target: O(rows * cols) — each cell is enqueued and dequeued at most once time, O(rows * cols) for the BFS queue in the worst case space. Push toward it with questions; never supply the approach or any program text.
